title: विमलकुमार सुवेदीको रोसा उपन्यास : मिथकहरूको पुनर्लेखन Bimalkumar Subediko Rosa Upanyas: Mithakharuko Punarlekhan
nepali: विगतका रचनाकृतिहरूलाई वर्तमान समयमा पुनः लेख्नु पुनर्लेखन हो । यसमा पूर्वकृतिका पात्र र घटनाहरूलाई वर्तमान सन्दर्भसँग जोडेर नवीन किसिमले प्रस्तुत गरिन्छ । विगतमा रचना गरिएका कृतिहरू वर्तमान समयमा सान्दर्भिक नहुने भएकाले त्यसप्रति आलोचनात्मक दृष्टि प्रस्तुत गर्दै नवीनताको खोजी गर्नु यसको विशेषता भएकाले उत्तरआधुनिकतवादी लेखनले यसलाई महत्त्वपूर्ण ‘टेक्निक’का रुपमा उपयोग गरेको छ । उपन्यासकार विमलकुमार सुवेदीको ‘रोसा’ उपन्यासमा पूर्वीय परम्परामा प्रचलित मिथकहरूको पुनर्लेखन गरी पाश्चात्य जगत्मा विकसित उत्तरआधुनिकतावादी चिन्तन प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ । सत्य शाश्वत र निरपेक्ष हुँदैन, यो समयानुसार परिमार्जित हुन्छ । समग्रताको अध्ययनबाट मात्र सत्यको नजिक पुग्न सकिन्छ तर मावन जीवनको निश्चित समयले समग्रतालाई बोध गर्न नसक्ने भएकाले मानवीय ज्ञान अपूर्ण रहेको छ भन्ने उत्तरआधुनिकतवादी दृष्टिको अभिव्यक्तिका निम्ति यस उपन्यासमा सिद्धार्थ गौतमको गृहत्याग, गङ्गा नदीको पृथ्वी अवतरण र कृष्ण–अर्जुन संवादको पुनर्लेखन गरिएको छ । यसमा परम्परागत मूल्य र मान्यताको आलोचना गर्दै त्यसलाई वर्तमान सन्दर्भानुसार परिमार्जन गर्नुपर्छ भन्ने विचारका साथै सामाजिक, राजनीतिक तथा प्रशासनिक क्षेत्रमा देखापरेका विकृत प्रवृत्तिप्रति व्यङ्ग्य प्रहार गर्न पनि मिथकहरूको पुनर्लेखन गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Rewriting is writing past literary works again in the present time. In this, the characters and events of earlier works are connected with the present context and presented in a new way. Since works created in the past do not remain relevant in the present time, its characteristic is to present a critical view toward them and to search for novelty, and for this reason postmodernist writing has used it as an important "technique." In novelist Bimalkumar Subedi's novel "Rosa," by rewriting the myths prevalent in the Eastern tradition, postmodernist thought developed in the Western world is presented. Truth is not eternal and absolute; it is refined according to time. Although truth can be approached only through the study of totality, because the limited span of human life cannot grasp totality, human knowledge remains incomplete; to express this postmodernist view, this novel rewrites Siddhartha Gautama's renunciation of home, the descent of the Ganges River to earth, and the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna. In this, along with the idea that traditional values and beliefs should be criticized and refined according to the present context, the rewriting of myths has also been done to launch satirical attacks on the distorted tendencies seen in the social, political, and administrative spheres.

Because works created in the past don't really stay relevant now, its thing is to take a critical look at them and search for something new, and that's why postmodernist writing has used it as an important "technique." In novelist Bimalkumar Subedi's novel "Rosa," by rewriting the myths that are common in the Eastern tradition, postmodernist thinking developed in the Western world is put forward. Truth isn't eternal and absolute, hey; it gets refined as time goes on. Even though you can only get close to truth by studying totality, because the limited span of human life can't grasp totality, human knowledge stays incomplete; to get this postmodernist view across, this novel rewrites Siddhartha Gautama's leaving home, the Ganges River coming down to earth, and the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna. In this, along with the idea that traditional values and beliefs should be criticised and refined according to today's context, the rewriting of myths has also been used to take satirical shots at the distorted tendencies you see in the social, political, and administrative spheres.
